summary: The day's dominant single-name event is EQT's all-stock acquisition of Range Resources (RRC), announced this morning with an 8-K covering items 1.01/7.01/8.01/9.01, which makes RRC a deal-driven name and leaves its 10-28 earnings estimate unreliable. Earnings risk is heavy this week: DORM reports today, EXLS/INCY/LOGI tomorrow, CALX/CVS/GRMN/RRC on 10-28, and AAPL/BDC/BJRI/HWM/LNG on 10-29 (AAPL possibly 11-02). All dates are estimates (last year plus 364 days), and the input's days_to_earnings counts calendar days, so I count trading days myself. Index and ETF risk stays elevated: oil near $117 on Friday, Iran headlines (Trump ruled out an immediate strike, futures higher), the Fed meeting and Big Tech earnings this week, AI-bubble worries, and Bitcoin sliding to about $80k.

event_risk.why: EQT agreed to acquire Range in an all-stock deal (1 RRC = 0.987 EQT; pro forma EV over $50B), with an 8-K 1.01 filed today. A merger-arbitrage setup; the price is now tied to EQT and deal approval, not to RRC fundamentals. The 10-28 earnings estimate is unverified and may be skipped or folded into the deal (the 10-14 8-K 2.02 flagged on 10-21 to 10-23 is still unread and is now secondary). Continues the open RRC date question from L2.

notable.headline: EQT to acquire Range Resources in an all-stock deal valuing one RRC share at 0.987 EQT shares, pro forma EV over $50B (8-K items 1.01, 7.01, 8.01, 9.01 filed 10-26)
notable.read: A transformative deal that overrides earnings and ordinary fundamentals for RRC. The price now tracks EQT, and the gap to the implied value reflects deal-completion risk (regulatory review, shareholder votes). The mega-merger framing adds a read-through to other gas names (GPOR, LNG indirectly). It also resolves the stale-earnings question as secondary, though the 10-28 results may still come.

notable.headline: Apple unveils redesigned iPad mini with 8.5-inch OLED, A20 Pro chip; iPhone Duo sells out amid long delays; Jefferies (Sell) raises PT to $270.62
notable.read: Product momentum is positive ahead of the Oct 28 event and the 10-29 or 11-02 print, and the Duo demand evidence is the strongest in the thread. Offsets: cautious sell-side from last week (Loop, MoffettNathanson), Thiel's critique (opinion), and Omdia's 20% y/y smartphone shipment decline. Headlines tagged AAPL about AI bubbles and breadth are market commentary, not Apple news; ignore them.

notable.headline: Instacart exploring a sale with preliminary talks with Uber and DoorDash (The Information, 10-23); halts differential pricing experiments (10-26)
notable.read: Takeover speculation from a single press source, unconfirmed, plus a regulatory concession on algorithmic pricing that echoes the shelf-label scrutiny on grocers (KR). Both are headline and deal risk for CART ahead of 11-09 earnings.

notable.headline: DA Davidson lowers Domino's PT to $382 from $423, maintains Buy
notable.read: A roughly 10% target cut is the first notable sell-side move on DPZ since the 10-20 buy. The rating is unchanged, so this reads as valuation or estimate trimming rather than a thesis break.

notable.headline: Pomerantz LLP investigates securities fraud claims against Mueller Industries after Q3 results
notable.read: Plaintiff-firm solicitations follow most stock drops and are weak evidence of wrongdoing. It continues the 10-20 print story (EPS miss, revenue beat) and matters only if a class action or an 8-K follows.

notable.headline: Wedbush raises VeriSign PT to $367 from $351, Outperform
notable.read: Post-earnings follow-through after Citi's $345 on 10-23; supportive, but the print is already known and this adds no new fact.

notable.headline: Citigroup lowers BJ's Restaurants PT to $70 from $75, Neutral
notable.read: A small cut three trading days before the estimated 10-29 print, in line with a cautious restaurant sector; the print is the real risk.

notable.headline: Incyte to co-fund Genmab's Phase 1/2 study of petosemtamab combination in first-line KRAS G12D colorectal cancer
notable.read: Early-stage pipeline collaboration, modest cash cost and long-dated payoff; it does not change the picture ahead of the likely 10-27 print.

notable.headline: RBC, UBS and Deutsche adjust Boston Beer PTs after Q3; RBC says volume growth remains weak despite margin gains
notable.read: Continues the 10-23 story of a volume guidance cut offset by a raised EPS floor. The sell side is split and confirms volume as the weak spot.

notable.headline: Walmart announces three holiday shopping events from Nov 12 to Dec 2
notable.read: Routine seasonal marketing, not material. The constructive sell-side thread continues, but stretched momentum is the more relevant caution; the 10-23 8.01 filing is still unread.

notable.headline: Retailers, including Kroger, face scrutiny over electronic shelf labels and dynamic pricing (MarketWatch, 10-24)
notable.read: A sector-wide regulatory theme that echoes the $5B price investment and the CART pricing retreat; no Kroger-specific action yet.

notable.headline: El-Erian warns of $150 oil if the Iran conflict widens; Burry backs Griffin on AI bubble and GPU overcapacity; futures higher after Trump rules out an immediate Iran strike
notable.read: Relief in futures this morning against a two-sided macro setup. Oil is the swing factor for the Fed meeting, mega-cap earnings and the AI-capex thread that dominated 10-20 to 10-23.

notable.headline: Bitcoin drops to $80,000; Bilello: Bitcoin and gold are 2026's two worst-performing major assets
notable.read: Continues the slide from the failed $84.3k breakout. Bears now cite $72k to $76k, and gold's break below $4,000 shows a broad lack of haven demand. No regulatory or exchange shock, so this is price action plus macro (Fed, Iran). Bullish bets (Alfred, Novogratz) are opinion.

notable.headline: Gold falls below $4,000 as yields rise ahead of the FOMC; extreme oversold and short data
notable.read: A 15% drawdown from the 8-25 peak with positioning stretched to the downside. A bounce is plausible, but the Fed decision is the next catalyst.
